questions.question: Which fields must match for two dense vectors to be meaningfully compared in one search space?
options: Embedding model and version, dimension, preprocessing, normalization, and metric contract
questions.explanation: Vectors from incompatible representation or scoring contracts do not share a reliable geometry, even when their arrays have similar sizes.

questions.question: Why keep an exact filtered search path during ANN evaluation?
options: It provides the ground-truth top-k used to measure ANN recall
It removes the need for labeled queries
questions.explanation: Recall@k compares approximate results with the exact neighbors under the same metric and eligibility rules.

questions.question: A postfiltered ANN query requests 10 authorized rows but returns only 4. Which metric exposes the immediate contract failure?
questions.explanation: Result completeness measures returned eligible slots divided by requested k; fast latency does not compensate for an underfilled result.

questions.question: Approximately how much raw storage do 2 million 768-dimensional float32 vectors require before index overhead and replication?
questions.explanation: 2,000,000 x 768 x 4 bytes is 6.144 billion bytes, about 6.1 GB before metadata, index structures, replicas, and build space.

questions.question: Why should an embedding-model migration build a separate index generation?
options: A new model always uses fewer dimensions
Old and new vectors may not share a compatible score space, and separate generations support evaluation and rollback
Separate generations remove all write amplification
questions.explanation: A blue-green generation prevents mixed embedding spaces and creates an observable checkpoint, quality comparison, cutover, and rollback boundary.

questions.question: What prevents an out-of-order update from resurrecting a deleted record?
options: A stable ID, source-version check, and tombstone retained through the serving checkpoint
questions.explanation: Identity and monotonic versions reject stale mutations, while the tombstone records deletion until every relevant serving copy has passed it.

questions.question: Writes arrive at 1,200 mutations per second while the indexer sustains 900. What happens without backpressure or added capacity?
options: The backlog grows by about 300 mutations per second and freshness degrades
The backlog remains constant because search replicas absorb writes
questions.explanation: A sustained 300-per-second capacity deficit accumulates in the mutation queue, increasing checkpoint and visibility lag.
